primary_claim: Sparse Concept Anchoring (SCA) — training-time geometric regularizers (hypersphere normalization, pairwise separation, and attractive/repulsive anchor/subspace terms on rare labeled examples) applied to a toy RGB autoencoder — enables selective, reversible suppression of a target concept (red) using only an anchor (R^2=0.99 for degradation vs. cosine similarity to red; cyan/orthogonal colors unaffected), and enables selective, permanent weight ablation of the concept only when repulsive isolation terms are added during training (unisolated ablation R^2=0.37, damaging cyan; isolated ablation R^2=0.98, no damage to other colors).

effect.metric: R^2 of reconstruction error vs. hue after suppression/ablation intervention
effect.value: anchored-only suppression: R^2=0.99, red error rises 0 to ~0.28 (theoretical 1/4); anchored-only ablation: R^2=0.37, damages cyan; isolated suppression: R^2=0.98; isolated ablation: R^2=0.98, red error ~0.34 (theoretical 1/3), no measurable degradation to other colors

depends_on: arXiv:2512.12469 (Sparse Concept Anchoring for Interpretable and Controllable Neural Representations)
stated_future_work: apply SCA to transformers, including deciding where in the residual stream to apply regularizers and whether interventions resist bypass via residual connections or attention
explore anchoring concepts of unknown/higher-dimensional shape using overcomplete subspaces
study many anchors at once and quantify where optimization landscape difficulty/task-performance cost begins as more concepts are anchored
pilot SCA on a real (frontier-scale) model
limitations_stated: tested only on a simple toy MLP autoencoder (RGB colors), not on transformers or language models
requires longer training runs in their experiments (96,064 samples for a simple model), though authors expect overhead to be modest for larger models
requires more hyperparameters (regularizer schedules with keyframes) to tune than standard training
concepts of unknown shape and many-anchors-at-once scenarios remain speculative/untested
quote: We think this is the most safety-relevant result in the paper: a concept, chosen in advance, removed permanently from a trained network by zeroing a known block of weights, with no post-hoc search, and with a reconstruction error close to a bound we can derive directly from the geometry.
